title: geogen control v1
description: How tools, tests and agents drive a geogen runtime, whichever engine runs it (Godot is the reference: runtime/godot/scripts/api.gd). The same commands arrive two ways. Live: newline-delimited JSON over a localhost socket, requests {id, cmd, args} answered {id, ok, result | error}, plus {event, data} lines for subscribed streams. Scripted: a script document (this schema's root) whose steps run in order once the world is loaded, each printing a stepResult line; then a scriptDone line, and the runtime exits (status 1 if a step failed). Points are [x, y, z] world metres ([x, z]: on the ground); angles are degrees; times are world seconds (they speed up with time.scale) and frames are physics frames. A runtime may add commands; one it doesn't have answers an error naming it.

stop_on_error.description: Stop at the first step that fails (default); otherwise run on.

point.description: [x, y, z] in world metres, or [x, z] on the ground.

start.description: How the world starts: applied before it loads (so a spawn primes what streams in first, and a load replaces the new game's start).

scene.description: The scene to load (default: the catalogue's).

day_length.description: Real seconds per 24 h of world time (0 stops it).

load.description: A geogen-save to start from instead of a new game.

set.description: {state key: value} set as the world loads (after a load).

give.description: {item: count} given to the player as the world loads.

stream_radius.description: Streaming radii (m): full exterior, LOD, interiors.

open_doors.description: Open doors matching this glob before the navmesh bakes, and hold them.

npc_limit.description: Spawn at most this many NPCs.

step.description: One command, with what a script adds: retry (world seconds to keep trying a step that fails, a physics frame apart) and an id to find its result by.

stepResult.description: A scripted runtime prints one per step run: `script: {...}`.

event.description: A subscribed stream's event: `script event: {...}` in a script, a line on the socket.

scriptDone.description: Printed after the last step run: `script done: {...}`.

const.wait: {seconds? | frames?} let the world run that much physics time (or that many physics frames)
const.batch: {commands: [{cmd, args}], stop_on_error?} run commands in order, one reply
const.wait_ready: {timeout?} wait until the world is loaded and the navmesh answers queries
const.world.info: scene, bounds, spawns, rooms, npc names, player spec, clock
const.world.query: {tag?, type?, name? (glob), uid? (glob), room?, interactive?, limit?} nodes carrying extras.geogen
const.world.raycast: {from, to} first hit: position, normal, node, room, interaction
const.world.nav_path: {from, to} navmesh path: points, length, reached
const.world.reload: {keep_player?} re-read the current scene's export (after a re-export)
const.world.node: {name | uid | node_path} one node: transform, world bounds, extras, colliders, children, interactions
const.world.lights: the light fixtures: {fixtures: {name: {visible, energy, range, y}}, total, light3d}
const.world.skeletons: skeletons (bone positions, skinned mesh bounds in the current pose) and animations
const.world.stats: engine object counts: nodes, orphans, objects, resources, nav_regions, bodies, world_children
const.player.status: position, yaw, pitch, eye, room, scene, pose, focus, keys, on_floor, walking; stream (chunked worlds)
const.player.teleport: {pos, yaw?} put the player's feet at pos
const.player.move: {forward?, strafe?, seconds} walk with the controls (until a travel point, then where it lands)
const.player.walk_to: {pos, timeout?} follow the navmesh there with the real body, opening closed doors on the way (a held key unlocks one) -> status: arrived | stuck | timeout | locked | refused, doors
const.player.use: {asset?, interaction?} use the aimed thing, or a named asset's interactions
const.player.lock: lock or unlock the aimed interaction with the keys the player holds -> {asset, interaction, ok, locked}
const.player.sit: {asset?} take the nearest (or the asset's) sit/lie affordance
const.player.carry: {prop?} pick up the aimed physics prop, or the one with that uid (glob) or node name, from anywhere: -> {ok, held}
const.player.drop: let go of what the player carries -> {dropped}
const.world.bodies: every physics prop: uid, node, position, center (of its box), yaw_deg, live, held, sleeping, speed
const.flows.list: spawned items (geogen/flows.py): {sources: [{uid, running, queued, emitted, alive, items}], items: [{id, source, item, mode, position, data, age}]}
const.player.keys: {keys?} set (or get) the keys given by --keys; held: those plus what the player carries
const.window.size: {size?: [w, h]} get or set the window size (headless runs too: layouts follow it)
const.input.key: {key} press and release a keyboard key by name (Q, F5, E), as the player would
const.input.mouse: {at: [x, y] (viewport pixels), button?: left | right | middle, double?: bool} click there, as the player would (a double click is a second press marked double)
const.interactions.states: every interaction's saved state, by stable id (<uid>#<interaction>)
const.interactions.set: {asset, interaction?, state, instant?, wait?} jump or animate to a state; wait: until the parts arrive, returning their bounds
const.interactions.use: {asset, interaction?, wait?} advance to the next state (honours locks)
const.interactions.lock: {asset, interaction?, locked} lock or unlock without a key
const.state.save: {path?} -> the game as a geogen-save (docs/schema/geogen-save.v1.schema.json): world and actor sections, clock, timers; interactions are instance state in world. path: also write it there
const.state.get: {key, actor?} a variable's value (world:pkg.name, actor:pkg.name, <uid>#<state>); actor: player
const.state.set: {key, value, actor?} set one, as a console would: rules and bindings react
const.state.list: -> {world, actors}: every stored value that differs from its default
const.quests.list: {actor?} every quest's state for an actor (default player): status, objectives (done | open | waiting, progress, markers)
const.state.load: {state | path} restore a save (one from before the format still loads); -> the save now
const.hud.aim: the crosshair: {visible, active (E would do something), focus}
const.hud.stats: what the scene's HUD stats and banner show (geogen/hud.py): {stats: {visible, stats: [{label, value, of?, text}]}, banner: {visible, text?, tone?}}
const.dialogue.show: the open conversation as shown: {open, dialogue?, anchor?, passage?, title?, text?, choices?: [{id, text}], selected?}
const.dialogue.choose: {index? (from 0) | choice? (id) | close?: true} choose one of what is shown, or close it; -> dialogue.show
const.hud.inventory: what the HUD's inventory panel shows: {visible, items: [{id, title, count, tags?}]}
const.inventory.list: {actor?} what an actor carries (default player): {items: [{id, title, count, tags?}], known: {id: {title, tags?, opens?}}}
const.inventory.give: {item, count?, actor?} give (negative count: take) items as a give / take effect would
const.inventory.use: {item, actor?} use an item the actor carries, as the inventory's F does: the rules' use_item event
const.hud.crossing: the pedestrian signal the player is at (on the kerb of a signalled crossing, or on it): {visible, crossing?, where?: kerb | crossing, state?: walk | flash | dont, text?, line?}
const.hud.quests: {track?: quest id | 'next' | 'previous', linger?: s} what the HUD's quest tracker displays: visible, tracked, title, status, note, active, lines [{id, text, state, optional, progress, progress_text}], waiting, clipped, rect, viewport; track picks the quest first, linger sets how long a finished quest stays up
const.hud.log: {open?: bool, select?: quest id | package/id | 'next' | 'previous', track?: bool} the HUD's quest log: {open, quests, sections: {active, complete, failed}, selected: {.., objectives}, tracked, hint, rect}; track makes the tracker follow the selected quest
const.hud.markers: {enabled?: bool} the HUD's world markers for the tracked quest's open objectives: {visible, tracked, markers: [{quest, objective, subject, kind: point | area | portal, position, screen, distance, on_screen, clamped, behind, radius?, inside?, scene?}]}
const.hud.notifications: {hold?: s, gap?: s, limit?: n, muted?: bool, clear?: bool} the HUD's toasts: visible, showing [{seq, kind: started | objective_done | complete | failed | notice, package, quest, objective, heading, text, age}], queued (waiting their turn, oldest first), raised, chimes, sounds (what rules played), hold, gap, limit, rect, viewport; hold sets how long a toast stays, gap the time between two appearing, limit how many are up at once; clear drops them all
const.npcs.force: {npc, option} make its next decision take that option
const.npcs.greet: {npc, wait?: s} greet it (wait: until it can be greeted, up to that long) -> {npc, ok}
const.time.pause: freeze the world (the API keeps serving)
const.time.step: {frames} run N physics frames, then pause
const.time.advance: {seconds, scale?} run S s of world time (at scale, default 8), return NPC reports
const.time.simulate: {seconds} run S s of world time at the current speed and report what it cost: {npcs, cost: {npcs, script_us, process_ms, physics_ms, physics_p95_ms, frame_ms, frame_p95_ms, frame_max_ms, draw_calls, primitives, objects}, traffic, trains}
const.time.clock: {time? 'HH:MM', day?, day_length?} get or set the world clock
const.time.skip: {until? 'HH:MM' | minutes? | hours? | days?} move the world clock forward (until: the next time it shows that); the rules' clock-time waits that come due on the way run in order
const.capture.screenshot: {path?, from?, at?, node?, view?, zoom?, isolate?, fov?, size?} PNG from the current camera, a pose (from/at) or framed on a node from a view (iso, front, back, left, right, top); base64 without path
const.capture.views: {node? | node_path? | bounds?, views?, zoom?, isolate?, path?} contact sheet of views framed on a node or box
const.events.subscribe: {streams: [events, interaction, npc, room, place, travel, traffic], types?, subjects?}: `events` is the whole bus (events.gd), narrowed to these types and subject IDs
const.events.history: {since?, types?, subjects?} -> {count, events}: the bus's last events (numbered from 1; since: only those after that number)
